title: Ang 1035: before creation
hookLine: for countless ages there was only darkness and the Formless (Maru Solhe M1, ang 1035)
tomorrow: how do you stop freezing when every face turns to you?

cards: When the power cuts out at night, there's a second of real dark. The fridge stops humming. The router light dies.
Your eyes reach for something and find nothing. A hand goes straight for a phone flashlight.
Guru Nanak, in one of his Maru Solhe on ang 1035, stays in that dark on purpose, and goes further back than any blackout: to before there was a world to light.

teach.b: The hymn opens, in paraphrase: for endless ages there was only utter darkness. No earth, no sky, only the infinite hukam, the order of the One.

teach.h: NO SUN, NO MOON, NO WORDS.
teach.b: No day, no night, no moon, no sun. The Formless sat in sunn samadh, a deep, absorbed stillness. Then it keeps taking things away: no speech, no air, no water, no being born, no dying, no coming and going.
Listen to how it's built. Almost every line is a no. The hymn makes you feel the empty space by removing each thing you'd normally lean on.
And yet it's never quite empty. Something is there in every line: the hukam, the One, absorbed and still. The dark isn't nothing.
It's full, before anything has a shape.

Later in the hymn the turn comes, again in paraphrase: when it pleased the One, the world was made. Light, sky and earth arrive only then, as a choice, not an accident. So the dark at the start of the hymn isn't scary.
It's the room before the lights come on, and someone is already in it.

how: Guru Nanak's Maru Solha on ang 1035, describing the time before creation, is sung in kirtan and often explained in katha as the Granth's account of what was there before the world.

o: where Nanak's hymn goes back before creation began
where Kabir describes the true warrior's drum
where Guru Amar Das's long Maru hymns begin

games.q: before the world — tap the pairs.
p: the order of the One, there all along
the Formless in deep, absorbed stillness

s: the hymn says that before creation there was simply nothing at all
no earth, no sky, no sun, but the hukam and the Formless were there.
almost every line of the opening is a 'no': no day, no night, no moon, no sun
the hymn makes you feel the emptiness by removing each thing.
the hymn says the world appeared by accident
in paraphrase: when it pleased the One, the world was made.

games.q: your friend's grandmother has died, and your friend says the silence in the house is unbearable, like nothing is left. which picture from ang 1035 might a Sikh friend offer gently?
o: the dark before creation wasn't empty; the One was already there.
silence means God has gone away until the noise comes back.
you should fill the house with sound so you never feel it.
games.why: Guru Nanak's hymn takes everything away, sun, moon, speech, and still the hukam and the Formless are there. the stillness is full.

practice: Rub your palms together until they're warm, then cup them gently over closed eyes so the dark is complete. Stay in that dark and notice it isn't empty: there's breath, a heartbeat, the warmth of your own hands.
Near the end of the sit, lower your hands and let the light come back slowly.

wordCard.voice: Ang 1035. Where Guru Nanak's Maru Solha goes back before creation: only darkness, and the hukam of the Formless.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: dhundhukaara, utter darkness; Guru Nanak's word for before creation (ang 1035).

carryVoice: Carry it: before the beginning, the dark was already full. Fifteen-seventy-two, lights coming back on.
